title.narrative: Responding to Critical Lean/Rainy Season WASH Needs of Affected Host Communities in Damboa

description.narrative:
ltpgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="line-height: 115%"gtThe ongoing food security and nutrition crisis in the BAY states of Northeast Nigeria requires urgent WASH interventions especially for households and communities with SAM/cholera cases to ensure that these affected people have safe and sufficient water, sanitation and hygiene, including through the distribution of WASH NFIs given the widespread poverty and the intensity of the lean season characterized by inflation and rising food prices.
The lean season coincides with the rainy season, increasing risk to children’s lives. This is when the incidence of acute watery diarrhea, cholera and other waterborne disease increases, as well as malaria and other disease, causing complications to malnutrition.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="line-height: 115%"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="line-height: 115%"gtFurthermore, the poor quality of water from available sources in the BAY States shows widespread faecal contamination with e-coli (WASHNORM 2022) with attendant poor hygienic practices remains a major source of concern. This poor access to clean and safe water sources increases the threat of diarrhea and transmission of cholera outbreaks that exacerbates malnutrition rates among children under the age of five.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gt
ltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gtThe 6 month host-community based WASH project aims to support the realization of the WASH Sector lean/rainy season priorities. It ensures support for lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtsevere acute malnutritionlt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gt (SAM) and acute water diarrhea (AWD)/Cholera vulnerable households, while ensuring the availability of sufficient and safe drinking water supply with free chlorine residual (0.5mg/litre) at point of use for affected communities. Stabilization centres shall receive enhanced support and services including training for personnel in monitoring chlorine levels, monitoring of communities with cases, then tracking these for hygiene promotion, NFI distribution, solid waste evacuation, and site disinfection.. The intervention shall ensure the functionality of gender-segregated sanitation facilities and solid waste management through monthly collection across dump sites in the host community while deepening hygiene promotion focusing on safe water storage, drainage cleanup, proper handwashing, proper food handling, and fostering the attainment of open defection free status especially in critical locations like lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtwater points, public spaces, and household level.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto line-height:normal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtApproximately 7,500 people out of the 38,264 out of camp population targeted by the WASH Sector in 2023 will be provided with sustained access to safe water through facilities upgrade/maintenance/optimization, regular water point chlorination (shock chlorination and bucket chlorination) and campaign with culturally appropriate hygiene messages in local languages at community level using approaches that include house to house visits and focus groups. Project shall engage in water quality control and emergency water treatment of turbid water for households with cases. This will also be emphasized in communities without communal water sources or relying on rivers and streams as their sources of water. lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto line-height:normal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltbrgtThe project facilitates the provision of safe water through sustained chlorination and the use of Aqutabs for household water treatment. FREE shall engage in the distribution of WASH kits with hygiene promotion, rehabilitation of water and sanitation facilities, composition and training of hygiene promoters and conducting hygiene and water treatment training at Stabilization Centres. Project shall engage in distribution of WASH kits for SAM households/communities, and self-monitoring by the affected households. Before upgrade of facilities, project shall truck water to New Estate area where critical gaps are causing conflict between IDPs and hosts. Project shall promote inclusion and protection, including systematic consultations with women and girls to expand their access and towards ending gender-based violence.lt/spangtltspan style="font-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgtlt/pgt
